newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to send health supplies to Tirana at weekend.
newsitem.headline: Italy to send health supplies to Tirana at weekend.

text.p: Italy said on Friday it was preparing to send emergency health supplies to Albania at the weekend at the request of Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.
It would be the first large-scale aid sent into the Balkan country since order collapsed and armed unrest broke out this month.

The foreign ministry said in a statement that the supplies, in the form of health kits, would be enough for 300,000 people for a month. A spokesman said Italy, acting unilaterally, would fly the aid to Tirana on Saturday or at the latest on Sunday.
The statement said Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini had approved "a first emergency humanitarian intervention for the Albanian people" in response to Fino's request.
The supplies will be flown to Tirana by military aircraft or helicopter and handed over to the health ministry for distribution to hospitals throughout the country.

The news agency ANSA reported earlier that Italy was moving 800 troops, including members of crack paratroop regiments and armoured units, to the southeast port of Brindisi in case they were required for deployment in a European Union relief mission.
The Defence Ministry has denied persistent media reports of impending Italian military intervention in Albania but had no immediate comment on the unsourced ANSA story.
"All I can confirm is that we are waiting for the European Union to meet and we hope it will take a decision soon," one official said.

EU foreign ministers meet on Monday in Brussels to provide a blueprint for security measures to assist a humanitarian relief mission in the wake of the violent unrest this month, sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes in Europe's poorest country.
Albania's new national unity government, formed last week in response to an armed rebellion in the south, has asked the EU to help restore order and provide food and medical relief.
The EU has indicated it will not back large-scale military intervention and the Dutch diplomat who led a mission to Albania this week said Europe should send a "modest police presence".
"Humanitarian aid is ready and could be delivered in two or three days on the condition of security," the EU's humanitarian aid commissioner Emma Bonino said in Brussels.

It is estimated that $10 million in basic medical supplies and 10,000 tonnes of flour are urgently needed. The U.N.'s food aid agency, the Rome-based World Food Programme, on Thursday sent a one-week mission to Tirana to assess relief needs.

Italy has played a key role in Western efforts to resolve the Albanian crisis and has taken in nearly 11,000 refugees who fled the chaos across the Adriatic Sea. It says they can only stay temporarily and will be returned when calm is restored.
The authorities repatriated more Albanian "undesirables" on Friday, bringing the total to more than 300, as bad weather at sea caused a lull in refugee arrivals.
Italy said on Thursday it had begun negotiations to reactivate navy patrols of Albanian waters to deter an exodus.

The ANSA report said Italian armed forces were preparing to make military units available to the EU as part of a multinational force and that military planners had identified three Albanian beaches where troops could be landed.
